original_question_en: Can every edge-colored complete graph have its vertices covered by few paths whose edges all share one color?
notes: PVW24 Theorem 1.3: for all n > 20^40, every 2-edge-coloured K_n has a vertex cover by at most sqrt(n) monochromatic paths all of the same colour. sqrt(n) is a real bound (i.e. floor(sqrt n)); paths may be single vertices and may intersect.
